Overview of 66degrees
66degrees is an end-to-end AI transformation partner that guides enterprises from complex business challenges to clear, quantifiable outcomes. Our company is the culmination of several successful firms, each a leader in its own right in cloud, artificial intelligence, and data. This convergence of talent and expertise is how we help businesses reach their own "inflection point," where chaotic data becomes a strategic asset, complexity becomes clarity, and AI becomes an engine for growth. Our ultimate vision is to be the catalyst for a future where every business operates as an intelligent enterprise, with autonomous systems unlocking human potential.
At 66degrees, we believe in thriving through challenges and winning together. These values not only guide us in achieving our goals as a company but also for our people. We are dedicated to creating a significant impact for our employees by fostering a culture that sparks innovation and supports professional and personal growth along the way.
Overview of Role
We are seeking a highly motivated and collaborative Associate Delivery Manager with a strong Agile and Scrum background to support the successful delivery of customer-facing technology programs across cloud, data, AI, analytics, and application development initiatives.
This role is ideal for professionals with approximately 3+ years of experience who have worked as a Scrum Master, Project Coordinator, Agile Delivery Lead, Technical Project Coordinator, or Associate Project Manager and are looking to grow into broader Delivery Management responsibilities.
The ideal candidate will play a key role in facilitating Agile delivery, coordinating cross-functional teams, removing delivery impediments, and ensuring timely execution of project milestones. You will partner closely with Delivery Managers, Product Owners, Architects, Engineering teams, and customers to deliver high-quality technology solutions while continuously improving Agile maturity and delivery excellence. In addition to supporting larger and more complex programs, you will also have the opportunity to independently manage smaller customer engagements as the Delivery Manager, taking ownership of planning, execution, stakeholder communication, and successful delivery.
Responsibilities
Delivery Coordination
Support the successful delivery of software, cloud, data, AI, and application development projects.
Coordinate sprint execution, release planning, project tracking, and delivery milestones.
Assist Delivery Managers in monitoring project health, risks, dependencies, and delivery schedules.
Track project progress, team capacity, resource allocation, and delivery metrics.
Escalate delivery risks and blockers proactively while driving timely resolution.
Ensure project documentation, governance artifacts, and status reports are maintained accurately.
Support multiple concurrent Agile projects and distributed engineering teams.
Independently manage smaller customer engagements as the Delivery Manager, owning end-to-end delivery including planning, execution, stakeholder communication, risk management, and successful project outcomes.
Balance responsibilities across independently managed engagements while providing delivery support to larger, strategic programs led by senior Delivery Managers.
Agile Delivery & Scrum Leadership
Facilitate Agile ceremonies including Sprint Planning, Daily Standups, Sprint Reviews, Backlog Refinement, and Sprint Retrospectives.
Coach Scrum teams on Agile principles, Scrum values, and continuous improvement practices.
Partner with Product Owners to maintain healthy product backlogs and sprint priorities.
Track sprint progress, velocity, burndown charts, and release readiness.
Identify delivery bottlenecks and work with teams to remove impediments.
Foster accountability, collaboration, transparency, and ownership across Agile teams.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives based on retrospective outcomes and delivery metrics.
Project Governance & Reporting
Prepare project status reports, dashboards, and delivery metrics for stakeholders.
Monitor sprint health, schedule adherence, defect leakage, resource utilization, and delivery milestones.
Maintain project plans, RAID logs (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, Dependencies), and action trackers.
Ensure compliance with delivery governance standards and organizational processes.
Support forecasting activities, release planning, and sprint commitments.
Stakeholder Management
Build collaborative relationships with internal stakeholders and customer teams.
Communicate project status, delivery progress, risks, and mitigation plans effectively.
Coordinate cross-functional activities to ensure alignment between business and engineering teams.
Support customer meetings, sprint demos, governance reviews, and project updates.
Serve as the primary Delivery Manager and customer point of contact for smaller engagements, ensuring effective stakeholder communication, governance, and customer satisfaction.
Maintain a customer-first mindset throughout project execution.
Continuous Improvement
Promote Agile best practices across delivery teams.
Encourage knowledge sharing, collaboration, and process improvements.
Identify opportunities to improve delivery efficiency, predictability, and team productivity.
Contribute to organizational Agile maturity initiatives.
Support Delivery Managers in implementing operational excellence initiatives.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field.
3+ years of experience as a Scrum Master, Agile Project Coordinator, Associate Project Manager, Delivery Coordinator, or similar role, with demonstrated ability or readiness to independently manage smaller customer engagements.
Strong understanding of Agile methodologies, Scrum framework, Kanban, and modern software delivery practices.
Experience facilitating Agile ceremonies and managing sprint execution.
Hands-on experience working with cross-functional software engineering teams.
Good understanding of Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).
Experience using Agile project management tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, or similar platforms.
Understanding of Agile metrics including Sprint Velocity, Burndown Charts, Cycle Time, Lead Time, Defect Leakage, Resource Utilization, Schedule Adherence, and Delivery Milestones.
Experience coordinating multiple workstreams within Agile projects.
Strong communication, facilitation, stakeholder management, and organizational skills.
Excellent problem-solving and conflict-resolution abilities.
Ability to work effectively in fast-paced, collaborative environments.
Exposure to cloud technologies (Google Cloud Platform, AWS, or Azure) is preferred.
Exposure to AI, Data, Analytics, or Application Development projects is an added advantage.
Preferred Qualifications
Certified Scrum Master (CSM), Professional Scrum Master (PSM), SAFe Scrum Master, or equivalent Agile certification.
Experience working in consulting, professional services, or customer-facing organizations.
Exposure to cloud migration, AI/ML, data modernization, analytics, or digital transformation projects.
Experience supporting distributed or global engineering teams.
Familiarity with delivery governance, release management, and Agile reporting.
Experience independently managing small to mid-sized customer engagements or end-to-end project delivery is preferred.
Passion for coaching Agile teams and driving continuous improvement.
Please note, we cannot sponsor or transfer any visas, of any kind, at this time.

Job Title: Full Stack Engineer (Contract)

Allocation: 40 Hours per Week (Full-Time)

Airtable helps organizations build the applications and workflows they need to run their most important business processes, without being constrained by off-the-shelf software. Its flexible platform combines a relational database, custom applications, automations, and AI, giving teams the building blocks to create solutions around the way they actually work.
Just like Lego blocks, what our customers can build with Airtable is virtually limitless. That flexibility is why more than 500,000 organizations, including 80% of the Fortune 100, use Airtable to power critical work across their businesses.
We’re builders at heart, and we’re looking for builders who want to expand what’s possible in Airtable and what the world can build with it.
We sell a powerful, flexible product to organizations with very different problems, teams, and ways of working. That means the best opportunities rarely come from following a script. We need someone who finds that energising—someone curious enough to understand how a business works, persistent enough to earn a prospect’s attention, and thoughtful enough to make every interaction relevant.
If you’re excited by the challenge of finding the right accounts, understanding what matters to them, and figuring out how to earn a conversation, you’ll thrive here. You’ll have the freedom to experiment, learn quickly from what works and what doesn’t, and build the skills to become an exceptional salesperson.
What you'll do
Run a hybrid pipeline motion: act on product-led signals early in the week, then shift into outbound prospecting for the bulk of your time.
Qualify prospects through calls, emails, and social media (LinkedIn) to generate sales-ready meetings for Account Executives.
Partner with AEs on our larger, more strategic accounts, shaping territory plans and outreach.
Build, test, and iterate on outbound strategies, using AI tools to work faster without losing quality.
Show up for a structured weekly coaching rhythm: pipeline and messaging review early in the week, skill-building (cold calling, qualification, objection handling) later on.
Deeply understand our customers' day-to-day pains so you can speak to them with real credibility.
Who you are
You bring the will; we'll teach you the skill. Hardworking, intellectually curious, and coachable matter more to us than pedigree.
You have grit and are comfortable with volume and rejection. Outbound requires consistency, and you show up for it every day.
You’re a strong written and verbal communicator. You can tell a story that shows you understand a customer’s needs and why Airtable is relevant to them.
You're AI-fluent, or eager to get there fast. We use AI tools throughout our sales motion, and you’re excited to learn how to use them to work smarter and more effectively.
Nice to have - in a EMEA wide team - if happen to speak fluent French or German in addition to English it is useful but not a requirement.
What we offer
The OTE target earnings for this role are £70,000 - £74,000 (depending on experience level) based at our EMEA HQ in Borough Yards, London.
We believe great work starts with feeling supported, that’s why we’ve built a benefits package designed to help you thrive both inside and outside of work.
Travel: £7,500 annual allowance to cover your commute.
Healthcare: Top-tier private medical, dental, and vision coverage through AXA, with heavily subsidised plans available for dependants.
Family planning: Up to £7,200 per year through Carrot to support your path to parenthood, plus a minimum of 16 weeks fully paid maternity or paternity leave.
Childcare: Save up to 42% per child annually through our Workplace Nursery salary sacrifice scheme.
Pension & protection: 9% company pension contribution.
Health & wellness: £150 every month to spend on whatever helps you feel your best, from fitness and mindfulness to hobbies and self-care.
Free lunch: Enjoy a varied, catered lunch every day you’re in the office.
Home office: £750 one-off allowance to create a workspace that works for you.
Time off: 25 days annual leave, plus 4 company-wide Recharge Days and additional time off between Christmas and New Year as part of our Winter Break.
Give back: 5 paid Volunteer Days each year to support causes you care about, individually or with your team.

Coordinate the activities of subcontractors to permit them to perform their work effectively and to integrate it with project schedules and progress
Inform all supervisors and subcontractors promptly of any construction schedule changes
Assist in the preparation of all job progress and cost reports to accurately reflect actual costs
Review and approve all requisitions, field purchase orders, invoices, and other significant reports and documents
Cooperate with the owner and his representatives, keeping them informed of construction progress
Cooperate with architects or owner representatives on an amicable basis, but in the long-term interest of the company
Hold job site meetings with project manager and the regional manager
Report regularly to the project manager to keep them constantly informed on job progress, plans, and problems that could significantly affect costs or schedules
Maintain a daily diary to permanently record all significant project facts, events, conditions, visitors, owner representative contacts, commitments, agreements, and approvals
Direct adherence to the company’s safety program in all phases and areas of the project
Make decisions under tight deadlines
Organize people, tools, and equipment and plan/manage multiple activities to accomplish desired results
Demonstrate leadership skills with ability and willingness to face challenges, direct others, and effectively address conflict
Exhibit commitment to quality by evaluating project-related processes, making necessary changes, using customer input to make improvements, and meeting/exceeding internal and external customer expectations
Act in a manner of integrity that shows support for the company, its values, and the employees while maintaining a constant focus on meeting/exceeding customer requirements and expectations
Necessary Qualifications:
Recent college graduate with a degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field

Proven experience as a combo welder and mechanical pipefitter in industrial or commercial settings
Certified TIG and Stick welder (must be able to pass weld tests)

Experience with equipment rigging and moving in plant/industrial environments

Experience in commercial or industrial laundry facilities or similar process plants
Familiarity with steam and condensate and other high-temperature systems
OSHA, aerial lift, forklift, or rigging certifications

A Day in the Life:
As a Construction Design/Build Project Manager (DBM) Intern/Co-op, every day brings a new lesson. You’ll gain exposure to the full lifecycle of a project while working alongside experienced professionals who are invested in your growth.
Here’s what you can expect:
Concept to Completion Approach – Gain how ARCO manages projects from the initial concept through final delivery.
Estimating and Takeoffs – Learn to describe project proposals and assign accurate dollar values.
Scheduling – Assist in creating timelines for subcontractors/trades activities.
Design Meetings – Attend meetings with the owner and design team, including structural engineers and architects.
Reporting – Prepare weekly reports, document progress, and track meeting action items.
Shadowing – Join project calls and site meetings to observe how our Design/Build Managers lead.
Buyout – Send bid instructions, schedules, and drawings to subcontractors. Evaluate proposals and assist with awarding subcontracts.
Permitting – Complete and submit permit applications with necessary documents and fees to city/county/fire authorities.
Shop Drawing & Submittal Review – Receive and route submittals to DBMs and communicate approvals to subcontractors.
Billing – Learn about subcontracts, change orders, pay requests, and pay applications.
Job Site Visits – Visit job sites with DBMs to monitor project progress.
Training & Learning – Attend offsite trainings and biweekly learning sessions provided by the Learning and Development team.
Business Development – Gain exposure to how we build client relationships and implement industry-wide business development strategies.
No matter where you’re starting from, you’ll leave this experience with valuable industry knowledge and a strong foundation for a future in construction.

Because ARCO is committed to creating opportunities for individual success, from day one, you will be given the tools to excel in your role, take on meaningful responsibilities, and experience why ARCO is truly the best place to build a career.
A Day in the Life:
A Co-op is an amazing experience where the student stays with ARCO for 6-8 months full time. The student will need to take the semester off school or reach out to their career services about their Co-op requirements. At ARCO, a Co-op has the opportunity to assist Project Managers with the following:
Estimating – Describing project proposals and assigning dollar values to the projects
Scheduling – Creating a working timeline for subcontractors/trades in order to complete the project on time
Design meetings – Attend design meetings with owner and team to understand design pro structural engineers, architects
Buyout – Send bid instructions, schedule, and drawings to subcontractors. Receive and evaluate proposals, then award the subcontracts
Permitting – Fill out permit forms, submit forms with drawings and fees, then send to city/county/fire and wait for approval
Shop Drawing and Submittal Review – Receive shop drawing or submittal from subcontractor, give to PM, communicate to subcontractor that they can begin ordering material and working
Billing – Subcontracts, change orders, pay requests, and pay applications
Job Site Visits – Visit job site with PM, make sure project is running smoothly
Necessary Qualifications:
Enrolled in Civil/Mechanical/Architectural or Construction Management Bachelor’s degree program
Minimum Grade Point Average of 3.0 out of 4.0
Previous Internship or Co-op construction experience preferred
Excellent verbal and written communication skills and a strong work ethic
What We Can Offer You:
At ARCO, we are committed to taking care of our greatest asset – our team. ARCO’s best-in-class benefits and superior compensation are what set us apart from the competition and continue to attract top industry talent.
Competitive hourly rate (with overtime possible)
Housing stipend (based on need)
Internship hours count towards our ESOP eligibility
End-of-term performance bonus based on merit
Path to full time position
Sign-on bonus for each term served if hired as a full-time associate following graduation
Direct access to leaders

Engagement events

job_title: Construction Project Manager Intern or Co-Op
description:
About You:
Are you a passionate problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment? Do you take pride in doing the right thing and delivering quality work with integrity? Are you excited to learn how construction projects come to life — from the first idea to the final walkthrough?
If you answered “Yes!” — this opportunity was built for you.
At ARCO Design/Build, we’re not just building structures — we’re building the next generation of industry leaders. Join us and discover what it means to be part of one of the nation’s top design/build construction firms.
A Day in the Life:
As a Construction Design/Build Project Manager (DBM) Intern/Co-op, every day brings a new lesson. You’ll gain exposure to the full lifecycle of a project while working alongside experienced professionals who are invested in your growth.
Here’s what you can expect:
Concept to Completion Approach – Gain how ARCO manages projects from the initial concept through final delivery.
Estimating and Takeoffs – Learn to describe project proposals and assign accurate dollar values.
Scheduling – Assist in creating timelines for subcontractors/trades activities.
Design Meetings – Attend meetings with the owner and design team, including structural engineers and architects.
Reporting – Prepare weekly reports, document progress, and track meeting action items.
Shadowing – Join project calls and site meetings to observe how our Design/Build Managers lead.
Buyout – Send bid instructions, schedules, and drawings to subcontractors. Evaluate proposals and assist with awarding subcontracts.
Permitting – Complete and submit permit applications with necessary documents and fees to city/county/fire authorities.
Shop Drawing & Submittal Review – Receive and route submittals to DBMs and communicate approvals to subcontractors.
Billing – Learn about subcontracts, change orders, pay requests, and pay applications.
Job Site Visits – Visit job sites with DBMs to monitor project progress.
Training & Learning – Attend offsite trainings and biweekly learning sessions provided by the Learning and Development team.
Business Development – Gain exposure to how we build client relationships and implement industry-wide business development strategies.
No matter where you’re starting from, you’ll leave this experience with valuable industry knowledge and a strong foundation for a future in construction.
Necessary Qualifications:
Enrolled in an accredited Civil, Mechanical, Architectural, Construction Management, Building Science, or Construction Engineering undergraduate or graduate program (other related engineering majors will be considered)
Excellent verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and a strong work ethic
Previous Co-op or Intern experience in construction preferred, but not required
GPA 3.0 or higher preferred, but not required
What We Can Offer You:
We are committed to the well-being of our associates and proud to be consistently recognized as a Best Place to Work.
Competitive hourly rate (with overtime possible)
Housing stipend (based on need)
Medical, dental, and vision insurance for Interns/Co-ops working at least 3 months
Company-sponsored lunches, happy hours, and networking events
Stocked kitchen with a variety of beverages and snacks
A welcoming, inclusive work culture - each office has an entertainment area

Treat people fairly and do the right thing
Understand our customers' business and solve their problems
Be positive, upbeat, and have fun

Are you looking to use your engineering background to solve client needs? Are you always thinking outside the box? Do you enjoy managing a project from start up to completion? If the answer is, “Yes!” then we have an opportunity that will impress you.
ARCO/Murray is looking for highly motivated Project Manager Interns who are passionate about the construction process to join the team for the Summer of 2027. At ARCO, every associate is empowered to drive their success. You’ll be responsible for project performance and profit from day one!
A Day in the Life:
ARCO offers an exciting Intern opportunity for highly motivated students. A Project Manager Intern will assist Project Managers with the following:
Estimating – Describing project proposals and assigning dollar values to the projects.
Scheduling – Creating a working timeline for subcontractors to complete the project on time.
Design meetings – Attend design meetings with owner and team to understand design pro structural engineers, architects.
Buyout – Send bid instructions, schedule, and drawings to subcontractors. Receive and evaluate proposals, then award subcontracts.
Shop Drawing and Submittal Review – Review subcontractor drawings with Project Manager and design team and communicate with subs on upcoming work.
Billing – Work with Project Manager to understand the business side of building such as managing subcontracts, change orders, pay requests, pay applications, and owning projects cost status.
Jobsite Visits – Visit jobsite with Project Manager and work with Project Superintendent’s to ensure the project is running smoothly.
Weekly Training Sessions – As an ARCO/Murray Project Manager Intern, weekly training sessions are provided to ensure the Intern team has a clear understanding of their role and how the business operates. Many training courses emphasize growing a deeper knowledge of building trades and how to leverage an engineering background to solve clients needs as a design/builder. Training is held virtually, in-person, at jobsites, and self-guided.
Necessary Qualifications:
Minimum GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0
Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s of Engineering program or related field of study
Prior industry internship experience is a plus
Extracurricular involvement is a plus
At ARCO, our first core value is to treat people fairly and do the right thing. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.
From recruiting, training, and hiring practices to selecting our subcontractors, we understand that diversity of all those involved in the construction process enhances our ability to deliver the best solutions to our customers. We hire the best and the brightest from across the country – constructing a team of experts in architecture, design, engineering, project management, and business services.
What We Can Offer You:
We are dedicated to the well-being of our associates and are proud to be consistently recognized as a Best Place to Work.
Competitive hourly rate (with overtime possible)
One-on-one mentorship
Structured training program
Opportunity to travel
Opportunity for term-end discretionary bonus

About You:
Are you a passionate problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment? Do you take pride in doing the right thing and delivering quality work with integrity? Are you excited to see construction projects come to life — from the first idea to the final walkthrough?
If you answered “Yes!” — this opportunity was built for you.
At ARCO Design/Build, we’re not just building structures — we’re building the next generation of industry leaders. Join us and discover what it means to be part of one of the nation’s top design/build construction firms.
A Day in the Life:
As a Construction Design/Build Project Manager (DBM), every day brings a new lesson. You’ll gain exposure to the full lifecycle of a project while working alongside experienced professionals who are invested in your growth.
Here’s what we will expect from you:
Lead Every Facet of the Project – Take ownership of project success from start to finish, including estimating, scheduling, quality control, billing, design coordination, cost tracking, safety, and proposal development.
Deliver Accurate, Impactful Estimates – Prepare detailed, reliable project estimates that lay the foundation for successful execution.
Collaborate on Vision and Innovation – Work closely with clients and design teams to shape preliminary concepts into high-impact, buildable solutions.
Influence the Big Picture – Participate in proposal meetings, helping to refine scope, reduce costs, and offer value-driven engineering insights.
Select the Best to Build the Best – Lead subcontractor selection and buyout, ensuring top-tier talent and cost-effective partnerships.
Drive Communication On-Site – Facilitate bi-weekly site meetings to align teams, resolve challenges, and keep progress on track.
Make Confident Decisions Under Pressure – Step up with calm, focused leadership when quick and effective decisions are needed most.
Juggle with Precision – Coordinate multiple moving parts to keep projects aligned with scope, schedule, and budget.
Champion Quality and Continuous Improvement – Monitor processes to maintain the highest standards and always look for ways to do it better.
Turn Feedback into Results – Actively listen to client input and transform it into outcomes that exceed expectations.
Lead with Integrity, Deliver with Purpose – Uphold our values in everything you do, ensuring client satisfaction remains the core of every project.
Necessary Qualifications:
Recent or upcoming completion of an accredited Civil, Mechanical, Architectural, Construction Management, Building Science, or Construction Engineering undergraduate or graduate program (other related engineering majors will be considered)
A strong interest in the construction process, specifically design/build, tilt-up concrete, industrial builds, etc.
Previous experience in construction preferred, but not required
GPA 3.0 or higher preferred, but not required
Proficiency using Word, Excel, Outlook and Microsoft Project
Excellent verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and a strong work ethic

Four core values that guide our culture:
Treat people fairly and do the right thing
Understand our customers’ business and solve their problems
Be positive, upbeat, and have fun
Create opportunities for individual financial success based on merit
Here’s what you’ll get as part of your employee package:
Competitive Pay + Industry-Leading Bonuses – Earn top-tier compensation with a performance-based bonus program that rewards your impact.
Ownership & Rewards – Choose between our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) or a generously funded profit-sharing plan— either way, your success is our success.
Secure Your Future – We offer both Traditional and Roth 401(k) options to help you build lasting financial security.
Invest in Education – Take advantage of tuition reimbursement for associates and up to $28,000 in scholarships per child to support your family’s future.
Recharge & Explore – Enjoy a fully paid 1-month sabbatical every 5 years, plus $5,000 to fund your adventure.
Give Back, On Us – Make a difference with 1 week of paid volunteer leave annually and a 100% match on your charitable donations.
Comprehensive Health Coverage – Access medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus 100% paid maternity leave for 12 weeks to support your growing family.
We don’t just invest in projects — we invest in people. From your first day, you’ll be part of a team that values growth, connection, and doing great work.

About You:
Are you a passionate problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment? Do you take pride in doing the right thing and delivering quality work with integrity? Are you excited to see construction projects come to life — from the first idea to the final walkthrough?
If you answered “Yes!” — this opportunity was built for you.
At ARCO Design/Build, we’re not just building structures — we’re building the next generation of industry leaders. Join us and discover what it means to be part of one of the nation’s top design/build construction firms.
A Day in the Life:
As a Construction Design/Build Project Manager (DBM), every day brings a new lesson. You’ll gain exposure to the full lifecycle of a project while working alongside experienced professionals who are invested in your growth.
Here’s what we will expect from you:
Lead Every Facet of the Project – Take ownership of project success from start to finish, including estimating, scheduling, quality control, billing, design coordination, cost tracking, safety, and proposal development.
Deliver Accurate, Impactful Estimates – Prepare detailed, reliable project estimates that lay the foundation for successful execution.
Collaborate on Vision and Innovation – Work closely with clients and design teams to shape preliminary concepts into high-impact, buildable solutions.
Influence the Big Picture – Participate in proposal meetings, helping to refine scope, reduce costs, and offer value-driven engineering insights.
Select the Best to Build the Best – Lead subcontractor selection and buyout, ensuring top-tier talent and cost-effective partnerships.
Drive Communication On-Site – Facilitate bi-weekly site meetings to align teams, resolve challenges, and keep progress on track.
Make Confident Decisions Under Pressure – Step up with calm, focused leadership when quick and effective decisions are needed most.
Juggle with Precision – Coordinate multiple moving parts to keep projects aligned with scope, schedule, and budget.
Champion Quality and Continuous Improvement – Monitor processes to maintain the highest standards and always look for ways to do it better.
Turn Feedback into Results – Actively listen to client input and transform it into outcomes that exceed expectations.
Lead with Integrity, Deliver with Purpose – Uphold our values in everything you do, ensuring client satisfaction remains the core of every project.
Necessary Qualifications:
Recent or upcoming completion of an accredited Civil, Mechanical, Architectural, Construction Management, Building Science, or Construction Engineering undergraduate or graduate program (other related engineering majors will be considered)
A strong interest in the construction process, specifically design/build, tilt-up concrete, industrial builds, etc.
Previous experience in construction preferred, but not required
GPA 3.0 or higher preferred, but not required
Proficiency using Word, Excel, Outlook and Microsoft Project
Excellent verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and a strong work ethic

Treat people fairly and do the right thing
Understand our customers’ business and solve their problems
Be positive, upbeat, and have fun
Create opportunities for individual financial success based on merit

Competitive Pay + Industry-Leading Bonuses – Earn top-tier compensation with a performance-based bonus program that rewards your impact.
Ownership & Rewards – Choose between our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) or a generously funded profit-sharing plan— either way, your success is our success.
Secure Your Future – We offer both Traditional and Roth 401(k) options to help you build lasting financial security.
Invest in Education – Take advantage of tuition reimbursement for associates and up to $28,000 in scholarships per child to support your family’s future.
Recharge & Explore – Enjoy a fully paid 1-month sabbatical every 5 years, plus $5,000 to fund your adventure.
Give Back, On Us – Make a difference with 1 week of paid volunteer leave annually and a 100% match on your charitable donations.
Comprehensive Health Coverage – Access medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus 100% paid maternity leave for 12 weeks to support your growing family.
We don’t just invest in projects — we invest in people. From your first day, you’ll be part of a team that values growth, connection, and doing great work.

This person is also tasked with bringing the project to completion on schedule, within budget and per the project specifications. The Superintendent is in charge of enforcing all Safety and Quality Control policies and procedures and adhering to and implementing all company policies and regulations.
Attend the post-award review meeting to receive project information and details for preplanning before construction
Participate with the project manager in preparing a schedule of construction activities and their sequence, the organization structure, staff selection, and the manpower and construction equipment requirements of the project
Direct and control the total construction project to meet specifications and within the allotted time schedule in an efficient manner to produce the expected profit
Assist the project manager/engineer in their duties, including prompt shipment of materials and permanent equipment and obtaining approvals of shop drawings and material samples
Coordinate the activities of subcontractors to permit them to perform their work effectively and to integrate it with project schedules and progress
Inform all supervisors and subcontractors promptly of any construction schedule changes
Assist in the preparation of all job progress and cost reports to accurately reflect actual costs
Review and approve all requisitions, field purchase orders, invoices, and other significant reports and documents
Cooperate with the owner and his representatives, keeping them informed of construction progress
Cooperate with architects or owner representatives on an amicable basis, but in the long-term interest of the company
Hold job site meetings with the project manager and the regional manager
Report regularly to the project manager to keep them constantly informed on job progress, plans, and problems that could significantly affect costs or schedules
Maintain a daily diary to permanently record all significant project facts, events, conditions, visitors, owner representative contacts, commitments, agreements, and approvals
Direct adherence to the company’s safety program in all phases and areas of the project
Make decisions under tight deadlines
Organize people, tools, and equipment and plan/manage multiple activities to accomplish desired results
Demonstrate leadership skills with ability and willingness to face challenges, direct others, and effectively address conflict
Exhibit commitment to quality by evaluating project-related processes, making necessary changes, using customer input to make improvements, and meeting/exceeding internal and external customer expectations
Act in a manner of integrity that shows support for the company, its values, and the employees while maintaining a constant focus on meeting/exceeding customer requirements and expectations
NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS
3-10 years of construction experience with a focus in commercial interiors (retail, restaurant, entertainment, etc.)
Computer skills: proficiency in using Word, Excel, Outlook and project scheduling programs
Possess and maintain a current, valid driver's license in your state of residence
Ability to meet the physical demands of the job, including but not limited to: standing or walking for long periods of time, occasionally on uneven terrain, bending, kneeling, crouching, climbing stairs, and/or lifting heavy loads of up to 50 pounds.
Able to organize people, tools, and equipment and plan/manage multiple activities to accomplish desired results.
Demonstrated leadership skills with ability and willingness to face challenges, direct others, and effectively address conflict.
Exhibit commitment to quality by evaluating project-related processes and making necessary changes, using customer input to make improvements, and meeting/exceeding internal and external customer expectations.
Act in a manner of integrity that shows support for the company, its values, and the employees, while maintaining constant focus on meeting/exceeding customer requirements and expectations.
Ability to travel across the country is required
Bilingual English and Spanish speaking is highly desirable.

ABOUT YOU
Are you someone who enjoys being hands-on, solving problems in real time, and seeing projects come to life in the field? Do you take pride in doing the right thing, leading by example, and delivering quality work safely? Are you eager to learn how construction projects are built from the ground up while working alongside experienced field leaders?
If you answered "Yes!" — this opportunity was built for you.
At ARCO Design/Build, we're not just building structures — we're building the next generation of industry leaders. Join us and discover what it means to be part of one of the nation's top design/build construction firms.
A DAY IN THE LIFE
As a Superintendent Intern/Co-op, every day brings a new lesson. You’ll gain exposure to the full lifecycle of a project while working alongside experienced professionals who are invested in your growth.
Here's what you can expect:
Field Operations – Gain exposure to how ARCO manages daily job site activities from site mobilization through project completion.
Safety Leadership – Participate in daily safety meetings, job site inspections, and learn how to promote and maintain a strong safety culture.
Scheduling & Coordination – Assist with coordinating subcontractor activities and monitoring progress to help keep projects on schedule.
Quality Control – Observe and support quality inspections to ensure work is completed according to project plans, specifications, and ARCO standards.
Site Logistics
Trade Coordination – Work with Superintendents and subcontractors to understand sequencing, resolve field issues, and maintain productive workflows.
Progress Documentation – Assist with documenting daily job site activities, taking progress photos, and preparing daily reports.
Project Meetings – Attend subcontractor coordination meetings, owner walkthroughs, and project planning discussions to see how field teams communicate and solve challenges.
Plan & Drawing Review – Become familiar with construction drawings, specifications, and shop drawings while learning how they are applied in the field.
Job Site Walks – Conduct site walks with experienced Superintendents to monitor project progress, identify potential issues, and verify work is performed safely and correctly.
Training & Learning – Participate in offsite trainings and biweekly learning sessions provided by the Learning and Development team.
Team Collaboration – Partner with Project Managers and field teams to understand how office and field operations work together to successfully deliver projects.
No matter where you’re starting from, you’ll leave this experience with valuable industry knowledge and a strong foundation for a future in construction.
NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS
Enrolled in an accredited Civil, Mechanical, Architectural, Construction Management, Building Science, or Construction Engineering undergraduate or graduate program (other related engineering majors will be considered)
Driver's License
Excellent verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and a strong work ethics
Previous Co-op or intern experience in construction preferred, but not required
GPA 3.0 or higher preferred, but not required
WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU
Four core values that guide our culture:
Treat people fairly and do the right thing
Understand our customers’ business and solve their problems
Be positive, upbeat, and have fun
Create opportunities for individual financial success based on merit
Here’s what you’ll get as part of our internship/co-op program:
Competitive hourly pay with overtime opportunities
Housing stipend available based on need
Medical, dental, and vision insurance for interns working at least 3 months
Professional development through training and mentorship
Company-sponsored lunches, happy hours, and networking events
Fully stocked kitchens with drinks and snacks
A fun, inclusive work environment
Annual Intern Summit where interns from across the company connect through leadership sessions, workshops, networking, and team-building activities
We don’t just invest in projects — we invest in people. From your first day, you’ll be part of a team that values growth, connection, and doing great work.

Support subcontract buyout, contract administration, change-order evaluation, and claims documentation.
Review potential changes for scope, cost, schedule, and risk impacts.
Partner with Project Managers and operations teams to ensure approved changes are reflected in budgets and forecasts.
Coordinate with Finance and project teams to resolve discrepancies and maintain accurate cost records.

Experience with general contracting, design-build, EPC, infrastructure, industrial, data center, or other complex construction projects.
Strong understanding of construction budgets, forecasting, subcontractor costs, change management, commitments, accruals, and project financial reporting.
Ability to interpret construction contracts, drawings, specifications, schedules, and cost information.
Advanced Excel skills and experience with construction ERP, project-management, or cost-control systems

job_title: Director of Business Development, Marine Terminal & Port Building Construction
description:
ABOUT YOU
Are you passionate about bringing clients’ visions for complex marine and port building projects to life through a collaborative design/build construction process? Do you have the industry expertise, relationships, and business-development leadership needed to expand opportunities across the marine building construction market? If the answer is “Yes!” then we have an exciting, long-term remote career opportunity for you. This position may be based anywhere in the United States and requires travel to client meetings, project sites, ports, and industry events as needed.
We are looking for a highly motivated Director of Business Development to join our team and lead growth within the marine terminal and port sector. This role is ideal for an experienced construction professional with 7+ years of experience developing client relationships, expanding market opportunities, and guiding complex Marine related pursuits from initial concept through contract award.
A successful candidate will bring a strong understanding of marine and port construction, including terminals, waterfront facilities, intermodal infrastructure, and related site development. You will build trusted relationships with owners, port authorities, developers, engineering firms, contractors, and other key stakeholders throughout the United States. You should have a proven business-development track record in Marine construction or engineering and the ability to consistently build trust with customers and colleagues alike.
A DAY IN THE LIFE
Identify, develop, and maintain relationships with port authorities, terminal operators, marine developers, industrial end users, engineering firms, and other industry professionals to generate new business opportunities.
Build ARCO’s presence and top-of-mind awareness within targeted marine, port, waterfront, and industrial markets.
Develop and execute a market strategy focused on priority geographies, project types, clients, and long-term growth opportunities.
Research and analyze economic, infrastructure, transportation, trade, logistics, and industry trends that may influence activity within marine and port markets.
Monitor upcoming capital programs, public and private development plans, procurements, and project pipelines to identify qualified opportunities early.
Attend port, marine construction, transportation, logistics, engineering, and industry association events to stay current on market conditions, competition, and client needs while establishing relationships with existing and prospective clients.
Build relationships with decision makers and influencers, understand their project goals, and position ARCO as a trusted design/build partner.
Provide ongoing updates to the ARCO management team regarding pipeline development, pursuit strategy, market activity, relationships, and key performance indicators.
Help develop and manage the execution of the sales plan, including goals, target accounts, opportunity qualification, and pursuit priorities.
Coordinate and manage the sales and proposal process with ARCO’s marketing, estimating, project management, preconstruction, and senior management teams.
Collaborate with internal teams to shape project strategies, assess risk, develop value propositions, and deliver compelling proposals for complex marine and port infrastructure projects.
Support the successful handoff of awarded projects to operations and project management while maintaining strong client relationships throughout delivery.
Travel as needed to visit clients, project sites, ports, industry events, and regional markets.
NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree required; Engineering, Construction Management, Civil Engineering, Marine Engineering, Design, or a related field is preferred.
7+ years of experience in business development, technical sales, preconstruction, project development, or a related role, within marine terminal, port infrastructure, heavy civil Marine adjacent construction, industrial construction, or Marine engineering and design.
Demonstrated knowledge of marine and port infrastructure projects, construction delivery methods, and the stakeholders involved in complex infrastructure development.
Established relationships with port authorities, terminal operators, marine developers, industrial end users, engineering firms, contractors, or other relevant decision makers.
Proven ability to identify opportunities, build profitable relationships, influence decision makers, and convert prospects into clients.
Experience working with economic development departments, port authorities, public agencies, infrastructure owners, or similar organizations.
Strong understanding of the design/build process, preconstruction, estimating, proposal development, and project delivery.
Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, organization, and relationship-management skills.
Strategic, self-directed, and results-oriented approach with the ability to work collaboratively across teams.
Ability to work effectively in a remote environment with minimal supervision.
Ability to travel as needed to meet with clients, visit project sites and ports, and attend industry events.
WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU

ABOUT YOU
Do you have an entrepreneurial spirit and a passion for alternative power solutions? Do you love solving for the complex power needs of large-scale construction projects? Are you looking for a company that is constantly trying to push the boundaries of what it means to offer a better construction solution by using design/build? If the answer is “Yes!” then we have an opportunity that will excite you. Who are we? We are ARCO, a Family of Construction Companies.
POSITION SUMMARY
ARCO/Murray is seeking an Electrical Engineer to support the design and delivery of
mission-critical facilities, including hyperscale data centers and other high-reliability
infrastructure. This role will include the development of practical electrical designs, the
coordination with internal and external project partners, and providing technical support
throughout procurement, construction, testing, and commissioning.
The ideal candidate is a technically strong, collaborative engineer who can translate
project requirements into coordinated, constructible electrical systems while maintaining
a high standard for safety, quality, schedule, and cost.
A DAY IN THE LIFE
Develop and review electrical designs for medium-voltage and low-voltage power
distribution systems.
Prepare and review one-line diagrams, electrical schematics, equipment
schedules, load summaries, feeder schedules, and design narratives.
Support the design of utility services, substations, transformers, switchgear,
generators, UPS systems, automatic transfer equipment, distribution equipment,
grounding, and emergency power systems.
Perform or coordinate load-flow, short-circuit, protective-device coordination, arcflash,
voltage-drop, and equipment-sizing studies.
Coordinate electrical designs with architectural, structural, mechanical, controls,
fire protection, civil, and construction teams.
Participate in BIM coordination, design reviews, constructability reviews, and
interdisciplinary page turns.
Review vendor submittals, shop drawings, RFIs, equipment data, and proposed
design changes for technical compliance and constructability.
Collaborate with procurement and project teams on long-lead electrical
equipment, technical evaluations, and supplier coordination.
Provide field engineering support during installation, startup, testing, and
commissioning.
Assist with troubleshooting, punch-list resolution, functional performance testing,
and turnover documentation.
Apply applicable requirements from the NEC, NFPA standards, IEEE standards,
local codes, and project specifications.
Communicate technical decisions, risks, and action items clearly to project
stakeholders.
Support continuous improvement of design standards, templates, checklists, and
engineering workflows.
NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline.
Approximately 3–8 years of electrical engineering experience; mission-critical, data
center, industrial, utility, or high-reliability facility experience is strongly preferred.
Working knowledge of medium-voltage and low-voltage electrical distribution
systems and emergency power systems.
Experience interpreting electrical drawings, specifications, equipment data, and
technical studies.
Proficiency with AutoCAD and/or Revit; experience with ETAP, SKM, EasyPower, or
similar analysis software is preferred.
Understanding of electrical construction methods, equipment procurement,
commissioning, and field coordination.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, schedule-driven environment.
Ability to travel to project sites as needed.
WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU
Opportunity to work on high-visibility mission-critical and energy projects.
Collaborative, design-build environment with direct exposure to engineering,
procurement, construction, and commissioning.
Professional development and opportunities for expanded technical and project
responsibility.
Competitive compensation and benefits package.

About You:
PureGrid Electrical is looking for a Project Manager who is highly organized, detail-oriented, and driven by flawless execution. You are a proactive communicator who thrives on coordinating the moving pieces of complex electrical projects, keeping a watchful eye on schedules, material tracking, and daily field coordination.
You excel at translating project designs into actionable plans for the field and managing relationships with clients, engineers, and subcontractors. If you are a collaborative problem-solver who values safety, accuracy, and schedule above all else, and you enjoy a fast-paced environment where you can take ownership of mid-sized industrial electrical scopes, you’ll fit right in.

Project Execution: Manage the day-to-day operations of mid-sized industrial electrical projects, ensuring tasks are completed safely, accurately, and strictly on schedule.

Necessary Qualifications:
Experience: 3–7 years of Project Management or Assistant Project Manager experience within the electrical subcontracting space. Exposure to industrial electrical or commercial design-build projects is highly valued.
Technical Knowledge: solid foundational understanding of medium-to-heavy industrial electrical work, power distribution equipment, and construction blueprints.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Electrical Engineering, or a related business field is preferred, or equivalent hands-on trade experience.
Software Proficiency: Strong proficiency with modern construction management tools; day-to-day experience using Procore and Bluebeam is required.
Skills & Approach: Highly organized with a structured work style, clear communication skills, and a practical, hands-on approach to keeping projects moving efficiently.
Travel & Location: Ability to travel as needed to support nationwide job sites during key project phases.

We are a growing national general contractor with a focus on light industrial, life sciences, advanced manufacturing, and mission critical projects throughout the country.
The Superintendent is responsible for directly managing the construction and administrative activities associated with the field operations of a project. This person is also tasked with bringing the project to completion on schedule, within budget and per the project specifications. The Superintendent is in charge of enforcing all Safety and Quality Control policies and procedures and adhering to and implementing all company policies and regulations.
A Day in the Life:
Attend the post award review meeting to receive project information and details for preplanning prior to construction.
Participate with the project manager in preparing a schedule of construction activities and their sequence, the organization structure, staff selection, and the manpower and construction equipment requirements of the project.
Assure that adequate manpower is provided as required to meet construction schedules.
Analyze construction equipment requirements and provide necessary equipment as required to utilize manpower efficiently, and release equipment when not required.
Perform material and quantity estimates for each phase of work.
Direct and control the total construction project to meet specifications and within the allotted time schedule in an efficient manner to produce the expected profit.
Direct and supervise the activities of craft superintendents and/or foremen in the performance of their regular duties.
Determine and convey to subordinates the most efficient construction techniques to be employed to assure quality and efficiency in construction.
Assist in the activities of the project manager/engineer in their duties including prompt shipment of materials and permanent equipment, in obtaining approvals of shop drawings and material samples, in preparing and submitting all change orders.
Direct all subordinates in promptly supplying all required accounting data, conforming to all company accounting and administrative procedures.
Coordinate the activities of subcontractors to permit them to perform their work effectively and to integrate it with project schedules and progress.
Inform all supervisors and subcontractors promptly of any construction schedule changes.
Review all request for change orders with the project manager to assure adequate provisions for direct costs, overhead, profit and time extensions are accounted for and are properly documented as well as that they are submitted promptly.
Assist in the preparation of all job progress and cost reports to accurately reflect actual costs.
Review and approve all requisitions, field purchase orders, invoices, progress payment requests, and other significant reports and documents.
Cooperate with the owner and his representatives, keeping them informed of construction progress.
Cooperate with architects or owner representatives on an amicable basis, but in the long term interest of the company.
Report regularly to the project manager to keep them constantly informed on job progress, plans, and problems that could significantly affect costs or schedules.
Maintain a daily diary to permanently record all significant project facts, events, conditions, visitors, owner representative contacts, commitments, agreements and approvals.
Direct adherence to the company’s safety program in all phases and areas of the project.
Become familiar with all company policies and adhere strictly to them in all activities and dealings, and require all employees to be aware of them and conform to them in their activities.
Carry out any additional responsibilities assigned by the project manager.
Working Conditions
The majority of work is completed on job sites in an office trailer or in an existing structure. Due to daily condition changes on construction projects, when employees are outside of the office trailer or structure they must wear appropriate personal protective equipment as required by the company's safety policies and as required for weather conditions.
Necessary Qualifications:
5-25 years experience as a lead superintendent on life sciences construction projects.
Able to make decisions under tight deadlines.
Able to organize people, tools, and equipment and plan/manage multiple activities to accomplish desired results.
Demonstrated leadership skills with ability and willingness to face challenges, direct others, and effectively address conflict.
Exhibit commitment to quality by evaluating project-related processes and making necessary changes, using customer input to make improvements, and meeting/exceeding internal and external customer expectations.
Computer skills: proficiency using Word, Excel, Outlook and project scheduling programs.
Possess and maintain a current, valid driver’s licenses in your state of residence.
Act in a manner of integrity that shows support for the company, its values, and the employees, while maintaining constant focus on meeting/exceeding customer requirements and expectations.

About You:
ARCO Design/Build is one of the nation's leading design-build engineering and construction firms, and our Advanced Manufacturing & Life Sciences Line of Business is at the center of the country's reindustrialization story. We build the facilities that make things: pharmaceutical plants, semiconductor fabs, precision manufacturing campuses, food and beverage production, and the advanced industrial infrastructure powering the next generation of American competitiveness.
We move fast. We think big. We hold ourselves to an exceptionally high standard, and we expect the same from everyone around us. Our culture is high-energy, high-trust, and deeply results-oriented. If you're looking for a slow-moving corporate environment with a well-worn playbook, this isn't it. If you want to be in the room where it happens and be the reason things actually happen, keep reading.
A Day in the Life:
This is not a support role. This is a force multiplier role.
The Office Manager & Executive Assistant to the COO and CCO of our Advanced Manufacturing & Life Sciences Line of Business is one of the most consequential hires we make. You will operate at the center of a fast-moving, nationally focused business unit, managing the calendars, travel, communications, office environment, and day-to-day operational infrastructure that allows our leadership team to perform at their absolute best.
You will be the first face clients, partners, and prospects see when they walk into our office. You will be the person our team looks to when the day goes sideways. You will hold the culture, own the chaos, and make it look effortless.
This role is for someone who is a proven operator. Someone for whom this is not a stepping stone but a craft. You have done this at a high level, you know it, and you're looking for an organization worthy of what you bring.
Executive & Calendar Operations
Own the calendars of the COO and CCO. Not just manage them, but architect them. You understand their priorities so thoroughly that you can make scheduling decisions exactly as they would.
Anticipate conflicts, protect focused work time, and build in buffers before high-stakes engagements so they walk in prepared, not frantic.
Prepare daily and weekly briefings that distill what matters into the essentials: priorities, context, and decisions required. No noise.
Gate-keep with grace. Every request for time is triaged, assessed, and handled with professionalism and discretion, whether the answer is yes, not now, or someone else entirely.
Travel & Predictive Logistics
Manage complex, multi-city travel with the precision of an air traffic controller and the foresight of a meteorologist.
You don't just book the flight. You check the weather. You confirm the hotel has reliable Wi-Fi for the client meeting happening 45 minutes after check-in. You have Plan B ready before the original plan has a chance to fail.
Own expense management for the COO and CCO with rigor and accuracy: timely submission, policy compliance, and clean documentation. You have done this before at volume and you do it without reminders.
Hiring & Candidate Experience
Coordinate the interview process for open roles across the LoB, including scheduling, logistics, candidate communications, and itinerary management for on-site visits.
Ensure every candidate who interacts with our office leaves with a strong impression of ARCO, regardless of outcome. You are often their first and most sustained point of contact, and that matters.
Partner with hiring managers and HR to keep the process moving without friction.
Fleet & Facilities Management
Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for our operations truck fleet, working in close alignment with ARCO's Enterprise-wide Fleet Director and their team. You execute at the local level; they set the enterprise standard.
Own the office environment at our LoB headquarters, from appearance and supplies to vendor relationships, service contracts, and lease coordination.
Ensure that when a client walks through our door, they walk into an environment that communicates exactly who ARCO is: sharp, professional, and built to deliver.
Review vendor contracts and office expenses not as bills to be approved, but as costs to be optimized. You have a bias toward ROI.
Events & Culture Activation
Plan and execute team events, client receptions, leadership offsites, and milestone celebrations that reinforce our culture and leave people energized.
Be the team's unofficial culture officer: the person who notices when morale needs a lift and acts on it before it becomes a problem.
Coordinate with marketing, leadership, and operations to bring ARCO's brand to life internally and externally through every touchpoint that flows through this office.
Communications & Brand Stewardship
Handle correspondence, client-facing interactions, and internal messaging on behalf of the office with professionalism, accuracy, and consistent tone.
Represent ARCO in every interaction, whether email, phone, or in person, as someone who embodies what this company stands for.
Systems, Process & Tech
Build systems, not band-aids. When something breaks, your instinct is to design a process that prevents it from breaking again, not just to fix it this once.

About You:
ARCO Design/Build is currently looking for an experienced Electrical/MEP Project Manager to join our team based in Charleston, SC. The Project Manager will play a key role as part of the General Services Charleston (Self Perform Team for ARCO Design/Build) team in delivering turnkey power solutions to our clients. This person will have the opportunity to lead managerial and administrative aspects of GSC projects including; estimating, scheduling, quality control, progress reports, progress billing, design review/coordination, cost reporting, safety, and proposal preparation.
At ARCO, every associate is empowered to drive their success. Project Managers at ARCO have complete responsibility for project performance, customer satisfaction, and taking projects from design to completion. Each Project Manager has full profit and performance responsibility for his or her projects and unlimited growth potential from day one.
A Day in the Life:
Create competitive, accurate, and timely project cost estimates and preliminary schedules for large pipeline of general electrical and renewable energy system construction projects
Thoroughly investigate the specifications, scope of work, drawings, and other RFP documents to develop a complete understanding of the RFP requirements. Demonstrate comprehensive understanding of the contract documents and the potential risks for a project
Participate in the proposal meeting with clients to review the scope of work, discuss ways to reduce costs, provide value engineering ideas, and negotiate contracts & fees
Oversee subcontractor selection and buyout process for all trades and vendors
Identify and investigate opportunities to procure material and/or specialty equipment directly when advantageous to project budget or schedule
Work with Project Superintendent to develop and review subcontractor scopes of work/contracts, project schedule, and site logistics plan
Lead preconstruction planning meetings with all designers, subcontractors and vendors aimed at solving potential constructability, sequencing, and/or manpower issues
Lead weekly/bi-weekly OAC meetings on-site once construction begins to review progress and address challenges directly with client
Track and manage project performance vs budget; prepare owner pay applications, cost status, and progress billing reports
Most importantly…find a way to make the construction process FUN for your clients, subcontractors, and vendors without sacrificing on quality or safety.
Necessary Qualifications:
BS in Engineering or related field; with a minimum of 3.0 GPA
2-5 years of electrical construction management or engineering design experience
Previous light industrial, manufacturing, or commercial project experience required
Experience using Procore, Bluebeam, Microsoft Projects and/or P6 preferred
Ability to travel nationwide as needed

Billing – Subcontracts, change orders, pay requests, and pay applications
Job Site Visits – Visit job site with PM, make sure project is running smoothly
NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS
Enrolled in a Civil/Mechanical/Architectural or Construction Management Bachelor’s degree program
Minimum Grade Point Average of 3.0 out of 4.0
Previous Internship or Co-op construction experience preferred
Excellent verbal and written communication skills and a strong work ethic

Organize, plan, and manage multiple activities simultaneously under tight deadlines and drive each project to 100% completion.

ABOUT YOU
Are you a passionate problem solver? Do you act with integrity and hold yourself and others to the highest standard? If the answer is, “Yes!” then we have an opportunity that will impress you. Who are we? We are ARCO, a Family of Construction Companies.
ARCO/Murray National Construction is currently seeking an experienced Project Manager to join our Mission Critical team in Chicago to focus on pricing and running data center construction projects nationwide. At ARCO, every associate is empowered to drive their success. Project Managers at ARCO have complete responsibility for project performance, customer satisfaction, and taking projects from design to completion. Each Project Manager has full profit and performance responsibility for his or her projects and unlimited growth potential.
A DAY IN THE LIFE
Lead and coordinate all managerial and administrative aspects of the project from the earliest stages of preconstruction through project closeout
Work closely with clients and the design team to develop preliminary concept drawings and project budget
Participate in the proposal meeting with clients to review the scope of work, discuss ways to reduce costs, provide value engineering ideas, and negotiate contracts & fees
Oversee subcontractor selection and buyout process for all trades and vendors
Identify and investigate opportunities to procure material and/or specialty equipment directly when advantageous to project budget or schedule
Work with Project Superintendent to develop and review subcontractor scopes of work/contracts, project schedule, and site logistics plan
Lead preconstruction planning meetings with all designers, subcontractors and vendors aimed at solving potential constructability, sequencing, and/or manpower issues
Lead weekly/bi-weekly OAC meetings on-site once construction begins to review progress and address challenges directly with client
Track and manage project performance vs budget; prepare owner pay applications, cost status, and progress billing reports
NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS
BS in Engineering or related field
3-10 years of construction management or engineering design experience
Previous experience leading data center or advanced manufacturing projects strongly preferred
Proficiency using Word, Excel, Outlook, and Microsoft Project
WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU
We are dedicated to the well-being of our associates and are proud to be consistently recognized as a Best Place to Work. Our compensation and benefits package not only supports our associates and their families but benefits local communities and communities around the world.
Industry-leading performance-based bonus program
Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP)
Traditional and Roth 401k
Tuition reimbursement for associates
Scholarship for associates’ children up to $28,000 per child
1-month paid sabbatical after every five years of employment, plus $5,000 for travel
1-week paid volunteer leave each year
100% charitable match
Medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage
Paid parental leave
Typical base compensation for the Project Manager role is between $84,000.00 and $160,000.00. Candidates with extensive experience may exceed this range. In addition to base salary, the role is eligible to receive discretionary bonus compensation based on individual and company performance.
